root.name: Bishop's Opening: Kitchener Folly
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 Nf6 3. d3 Be7 4. Nf3 O-O

overview: A quiet Italian-style set-up: White keeps the bishop on c4, plays d3 and Nf3, and Black castles with ...Be7. The usual plan is c3, Nbd2 and a later d4 or a slow build-up. It is unforced and low in theory, an easy line to play at club level.

white_ideas.idea: Play c3, Nbd2 and castle, preparing d4 or Re1 and Nf1-g3
Keep the c4 bishop aimed at f7

black_ideas.idea: Reach ...d6, ...Nc6 and ...Bg4 or ...Re8 with a solid centre
Strike with ...d5 when the bishop leaves

typical_structures.structure: Giuoco Pianissimo-type centre with d3 and e4 against e5 and d6
Tension that is not resolved early

character.notes: Quiet, slow manoeuvring with no early tactics.

structure.notes: The centre stays in tension with no pawn trades.

level.notes: A clear plan and almost no theory.

plan_phrases: slow build-up with c3 and d4

character.reason: Both sides develop slowly and neither can be hit quickly.

structure.reason: The e4/e5 centre stays in tension, like the Giuoco Pianissimo.

approach.reason: It is a respectable Italian-type set-up but depends on the opponent.

level.reason: Clear plans and little to memorise, like the Pianissimo.

plans.reason: No distinctive plan beyond normal Italian development.
